properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 2:46PM MDT until August 30 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Garfield County in southern Utah...
Northeastern Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 745 PM MDT.

* At 246 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across primarily Brimhall Natural Bridge near Halls
Creek. Water will continue to flow downstream through Halls Creek
Narrows down to Lake Powell. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons,  and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Brimhall Natural Bridge near Halls Creek, with water continuing to
flow down Halls Creek into Halls Creek Narrows and down to Lake
Powell.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 7:45 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 7:45 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 1:33PM MST until August 30 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Antelope Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 500 PM MST /600 PM MDT/.

* At 133 PM MST /233 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the Antelope Creek basin. Between 0.5 and
1 inch of rain has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to
0.75 inches are possible with approaching storms in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Antelope Creek basin.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Antelope Creek basin.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rattlesnake Canyon, Owl Canyon, Upper Antelope Canyon, Lower
Antelope Canyon, Porcupine Canyon, Mountain Sheep Canyon, LeChee
and Wind Pebble Canyon.

This includes the following slot canyons...
Upper Antelope Canyon, Lower Antelope Canyon, Owl Canyon, Rattlesnake
Canyon and Porcupine Canyon.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Antelope Creek.
properties.instruction:
Get out of Antelope Canyon and other area slot canyons immediately!
Deadly flash flooding is imminent or occurring!

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 5:00 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 1:32PM MST until August 30 at 2:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 132 PM MST /232 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area, near Marble Canyon.
Between 0.75 and 1.75 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall
amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marble Canyon, Marble Canyon Airport, Jackass Canyon, Horseshoe
Bend and Lees Ferry.

This includes the following highways...
U.S. Highway 89 between mile markers 543 and 546. the Colorado River
between river miles 0 and 11. U.S. Highway 89A between mile markers
531 and 545.

This includes the following slot canyons...
Cathedral Wash, Cathedral Wash and Jackass Canyon.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lee's Ferry Campground, Lees Ferry Campground, Paria Beach Camp Site,
Opposite Cathedral Camp Site, Cathedral Wash Camp Site, Jackass Camp
Site, Badger Camp Site, Sandbar Camp Site, Soap Creek Camp Site,
Ferry Swale Camp Site, Twin Stripes Camp Site and Lees Ferry Camp
Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Ferry Swale Canyon, Cave Canyon, Ninemile Draw, Salt Water Wash,
Fall Creek, Cathedral Wash, Colorado River, Honey Draw, Seven Mile
Draw, Water Holes Canyon, "5- Mile Wash", Paria River, Jackass
Creek, Badger Canyon and Soap Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 2:28PM MDT until August 30 at 9:30PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 930 PM MDT Sunday.

* At 228 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of normally dry washes,
slot canyons, streams, creeks and rivers.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bryce Canyon National Park, Buckskin Wash, Wire Pass, the Paria
River, Paria River Canyon, Bull Valley Gorge, and Willis Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.
